This is a well-structured, accessible HTML5 document demonstrating modern best practices for semantic markup and inclusive design.

It uses semantic landmarks, a skip link for keyboard navigation, and CSS that adapts to your light or dark mode preference.

Text and link colors meet WCAG AA contrast in both themes, type scales with your browser's font size, and motion respects your system settings.

Features

  • Semantic HTML structure with proper landmarks
  • Keyboard accessible navigation and focus management
  • Dark mode support with custom color schemes
  • Responsive typography using modern CSS
  • Print-friendly styles for better readability
  • WCAG AA contrast compliance in all color modes

Examples

Component Cards

Card components are useful for organizing related content. They include a subtle border and padding for visual separation.

Learn more about accessibility resources

Interactive Elements

Buttons and links are fully accessible with clear focus states. All interactive elements include visible focus indicators and proper ARIA labels.

Keyboard navigation: Use Tab to move forward, Shift+Tab to move backward, and Enter or Space to activate.

Accessible Form

Fields marked * are required.

For example, name@example.com

content.text:
`0.html` was already well built. The semantics, ARIA, contrast, focus styles, reduced-motion, forced-colors, dark mode and print styles all held up when I read through them, so I only made a few small fixes rather than reworking it. I haven't opened the page in a browser to check them. My first attempt ran a script through the shell, and that was blocked because it needed an approval that couldn't be given here. I made the same changes with direct file edits instead: 1. **Heading:** Changed the vague `

Welcome

` to `Accessible HTML5 Guide` so it matches the page title and the structured data. Screen-reader users often jump straight to the h1, so a descriptive one helps them. 2. **Removed duplicate Twitter tags:** Twitter/X uses the `og:title` and `og:description` tags when its own are missing, so `twitter:title` and `twitter:description` added nothing. 3. **Removed four `dns-prefetch` hints:** They only pointed to the Resources links, which open in a new tab when clicked. They made the browser look up those addresses on every page load for almost no benefit. 4. **Copyright line:** It had no owner ("© 2026. All rights reserved."). It now reads "© 2026 K. Smith. All rights reserved." 5. **Script safety:** The form's submit handler used `messageInput` without checking it existed, unlike the rest of the script. It's now checked, so the handler won't crash if the message field is ever removed. The canonical URL is still `https://www.example.com`, which is a placeholder. Replace it with the real address before you publish.
